layers.note: A grass of open woods, forest edges, clearings and oak stands.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

shade_tolerance.note: Grows in part shade or sun.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −12 °C, gone by −20 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Cold-hardy: lows to about −34 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −42 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 12.5 to 26 °C; gone below 10 °C, where summers are too short, and above 30 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,800 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,100.

degree_days_5.note: About 800 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 400: from the lowlands to the montane forest.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.3, gone by 0.2.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; its range takes in summer-dry coasts and interior mountains with some summer rain, to about 0.45 of the year's precipitation.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Blue wildrye grows from Alaska to Mexico and east to the Great Plains (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
